title: Convenience vs health the takeaway dilemma
titleChinese: 图省事还是保健康？点外卖的纠结
paragraphs: Feeling hungry? If you’re feeling peckish or famished, what’s the easiest way to satisfy your hunger? Many of us will reach for a takeaway menu and order some delicious – but possibly unhealthy – food. And our increasingly busy and hectic lives add to our need to buy ready-made food on the go or delivered to home.

Eating options are endless, and new technology means we can feed our cravings at the push of a button. Takeaway delivery apps make ordering food quick and convenient, and during the recent coronavirus crisis, it provided a lifeline to those stuck at home with nothing to cook or who lacked the skills to prepare a meal for themselves. It’s estimated that in the UK alone, people eat three million takeaway meals a day, and the three biggest delivery apps together offer a choice of 100 cuisines from 60,000 restaurants. Amelia Brophy, Head of UK Data Products at YouGov, told the BBC that its research “suggests that the frequency of takeaways ordered is expected to increase in the future.”

It’s no wonder we are tempted to skip the grocery shopping, bypass the kitchen, and tuck into something that someone else has prepared. But ordering a deep crust pizza, a spicy curry or a box of noodles, can come at a price both financially and to our health. Eating too much processed and unhealthy fast food has some effect on obesity and the risk of developing certain metabolic and cardiovascular diseases. A few years ago, The BBC Good Food Nation Survey found that most people ate fast food on average two days per week. But, in the 16 to 20-year-old category, one in six ate fast food at least twice a day.

Of course, reducing salt, sugar and fat is one way to make takeaway food healthier, as well as offering smaller portion sizes. But the best advice you might want to take away from this Takeaway English is to find a recipe book and try making your own nutritious meal. And if you haven’t got time, try ordering a healthier alternative from the menu.

vocabulary.entry: peckish /ˈpekɪʃ/ adj. 有点饿的（口语）
vocabulary.example: I'm feeling a bit peckish – let's have some biscuits.
vocabulary.translation: 我有点饿了，我们吃点饼干吧。

vocabulary.entry: famished /ˈfæmɪʃt/ adj. 极饿的；饿得慌的
vocabulary.example: After the hike, we were absolutely famished.
vocabulary.translation: 徒步旅行结束后，我们饿得不行。

vocabulary.entry: takeaway /ˈteɪkəweɪ/ n. 外卖食物
vocabulary.example: We ordered a Chinese takeaway for dinner.
vocabulary.translation: 我们晚餐点了一份中式外卖。

vocabulary.entry: hectic /ˈhektɪk/ adj. 忙碌的；忙乱的
vocabulary.example: She has a hectic schedule with work and family commitments.
vocabulary.translation: 她的日程很忙，既要工作又要照顾家庭。

vocabulary.entry: ready-made /ˌredi ˈmeɪd/ adj. 现成的；做好的
vocabulary.example: Ready-made meals are convenient for busy people.
vocabulary.translation: 现成的饭菜对忙碌的人来说很方便。

vocabulary.entry: on the go /ɒn ðə ɡəʊ/ 忙个不停；在路上（俚语）
vocabulary.example: I eat breakfast on the go every morning.
vocabulary.translation: 我每天早上都在路上吃早餐。

vocabulary.entry: craving /ˈkreɪvɪŋ/ n. 渴望；渴求
vocabulary.example: She has a craving for chocolate cake.
vocabulary.translation: 她特别想吃巧克力蛋糕。

vocabulary.term: at the push of a button
vocabulary.entry: at the push of a button /æt ðə pʊʃ ɒv ə ˈbʌtn/ 轻轻一按；轻而易举
vocabulary.example: We can access information at the push of a button.
vocabulary.translation: 我们轻轻一按就能获取信息。

vocabulary.entry: lifeline /ˈlaɪflaɪn/ n. 生命线；救命稻草
vocabulary.example: The charity provides a lifeline for homeless people.
vocabulary.translation: 这家慈善机构为无家可归的人提供了一条生命线。

vocabulary.entry: cuisine /kwɪˈziːn/ n. 风味；烹饪风格
vocabulary.example: Italian cuisine is famous for its pasta and pizza.
vocabulary.translation: 意大利菜以其面食和披萨而闻名。

vocabulary.entry: frequency /ˈfriːkwənsi/ n. 频率；频次
vocabulary.example: The frequency of bus services will be increased next month.
vocabulary.translation: 下个月公交车的发车频次将会增加。

vocabulary.entry: tempt /tempt/ v. 诱惑；吸引
vocabulary.example: The smell of fresh bread tempted me into the bakery.
vocabulary.translation: 新鲜面包的香味诱使我走进了面包店。

vocabulary.entry: skip /skɪp/ v. 跳过；略过
vocabulary.example: I decided to skip breakfast this morning because I was late.
vocabulary.translation: 今天早上我迟到了，所以决定不吃早餐。

vocabulary.entry: bypass /ˈbaɪpɑːs/ v. 绕过；避开
vocabulary.example: We can bypass the town centre by taking the ring road.
vocabulary.translation: 我们可以走环城公路绕过市中心。

vocabulary.entry: tuck into /tʌk ˈɪntuː/ 狼吞虎咽地吃；大快朵颐（俚语）
vocabulary.example: The children tucked into the birthday cake eagerly.
vocabulary.translation: 孩子们迫不及待地大口吃起了生日蛋糕。

vocabulary.entry: come at a price /kʌm æt ə praɪs/ 付出代价；有负面影响
vocabulary.example: Success often comes at a price.
vocabulary.translation: 成功往往是要付出代价的。

vocabulary.entry: processed food /ˈprəʊsest fuːd/ 加工食品
vocabulary.example: Eating too much processed food is bad for your health.
vocabulary.translation: 吃太多加工食品对健康有害。

vocabulary.entry: obesity /əʊˈbiːsəti/ n. 肥胖症
vocabulary.example: Lack of exercise can lead to obesity.
vocabulary.translation: 缺乏运动可能会导致肥胖症。

vocabulary.entry: metabolic disease /ˌmetəˈbɒlɪk dɪˈziːz/ 代谢性疾病
vocabulary.example: Diabetes is a common metabolic disease.
vocabulary.translation: 糖尿病是一种常见的代谢性疾病。

vocabulary.entry: cardiovascular disease /ˌkɑːdiəʊˈvæskjələ dɪˈziːz/ 心血管疾病
vocabulary.example: Smoking increases the risk of cardiovascular disease.
vocabulary.translation: 吸烟会增加患心血管疾病的风险。

vocabulary.entry: portion size /ˈpɔːʃn saɪz/ 份餐量；分量
vocabulary.example: Restaurants should offer smaller portion sizes to reduce waste.
vocabulary.translation: 餐厅应该提供小份餐食，以减少浪费。

vocabulary.entry: nutritious /njuˈtrɪʃəs/ adj. 有营养的；营养丰富的
vocabulary.example: Fruit and vegetables are very nutritious.
vocabulary.translation: 水果和蔬菜富含营养。

sentences.chinese: 要是你有点饥肠辘辘或是饿得前胸贴后背，满足食欲最简单的办法是什么呢？

sentences.english: Many of us will reach for a takeaway menu and order some delicious – but possibly unhealthy – food.
sentences.chinese: 很多人会拿起外卖菜单，点上一些美味却可能不太健康的食物。

sentences.english: And our increasingly busy and hectic lives add to our need to buy ready-made food on the go or delivered to home.
sentences.chinese: 如今我们的生活越来越忙碌紧凑，这也让我们更需要购买现成的食物，要么在外随手解决，要么直接配送到家。

sentences.english: Eating options are endless, and new technology means we can feed our cravings at the push of a button.
sentences.chinese: 吃的选择数不胜数，新技术的发展更是让我们只需按一下按钮，就能满足口腹之欲。

sentences.english: It’s estimated that in the UK alone, people eat three million takeaway meals a day, and the three biggest delivery apps together offer a choice of 100 cuisines from 60,000 restaurants.

sentences.english: Amelia Brophy, Head of UK Data Products at YouGov, told the BBC that its research “suggests that the frequency of takeaways ordered is expected to increase in the future.”
sentences.chinese: 舆观调查网英国数据产品主管阿米莉亚·布罗菲在接受BBC采访时表示，他们的研究显示“未来外卖的下单频率预计还会上升”。

sentences.english: It’s no wonder we are tempted to skip the grocery shopping, bypass the kitchen, and tuck into something that someone else has prepared.
sentences.chinese: 难怪我们会忍不住想跳过买菜这一步，绕开厨房，直接大快朵颐别人做好的饭菜。

sentences.english: But ordering a deep crust pizza, a spicy curry or a box of noodles, can come at a price both financially and to our health.
sentences.chinese: 但点一份厚底披萨、一份辛辣咖喱或是一盒面条，代价是双重的——既花钱，又损害健康。

sentences.english: Eating too much processed and unhealthy fast food has some effect on obesity and the risk of developing certain metabolic and cardiovascular diseases.
sentences.chinese: 吃太多加工过的不健康快餐，会增加肥胖风险，还可能诱发某些代谢性疾病和心血管疾病。

sentences.english: A few years ago, The BBC Good Food Nation Survey found that most people ate fast food on average two days per week.
sentences.chinese: 几年前，《BBC美食国度调查报告》发现，大多数人平均每周吃两天快餐。

sentences.english: But, in the 16 to 20-year-old category, one in six ate fast food at least twice a day.
sentences.chinese: 而在16到20岁的年龄段，六分之一的人每天至少吃两次快餐。

sentences.english: Of course, reducing salt, sugar and fat is one way to make takeaway food healthier, as well as offering smaller portion sizes.

sentences.english: But the best advice you might want to take away from this Takeaway English is to find a recipe book and try making your own nutritious meal.
sentences.chinese: 不过，从这篇“外卖英语”里，你能得到的最佳建议是：找一本食谱，试着自己做一顿营养均衡的饭菜。

sentences.english: And if you haven’t got time, try ordering a healthier alternative from the menu.
sentences.chinese: 要是实在没时间，那就从菜单上选一个更健康的菜品吧。
